assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Discount?' or 'Expected?')
Table has exactly 3 data rows (GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)
Test method body contains only one assertEquals (or equivalent assertion) — not three
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column

Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case (e.g. 'discountByCustomerTier' → 'Discount By Customer Tier'). Not a generic name like 'test1' or 'testMethod'.

If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as fixed values shared by all rows, where/when the rule applies, or open questions. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context (e.g. fixed values are included as a column rather than hardcoded in the method body).
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
The build file (pom.xml) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit:1.2.1 as a test dependency
The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
The generated tests pass when executed against DiscountService
